how.meta.title: How it works · Kobo The Wolf
how.meta.description: How kobothewolf.com and the KOBO.EXE card editor are built: architecture, your data, exports, security, quality and releases.
how.title: How it works
how.lead: The technical tour of this site and its card editor, for the curious. Each section links to the documents and code it summarizes.
how.overview.title: Overview
how.overview.p1: kobothewolf.com is two things on one page: a short profile, and the KOBO.EXE card editor, where you design a print-ready business card in the boykisser-uwu style and download it.
how.overview.p2: It's a static site on GitHub Pages: no server, no database, no account. Everything you do happens in your browser.
how.architecture.title: Architecture
how.architecture.p1: The page is built with Vite. The profile is plain HTML whose text is filled from the language catalogs at build time, so it reads even without JavaScript. The editor is a separate Preact bundle that loads only after the page has painted, so the profile never waits for it.
how.architecture.p2: Cards are data, not code. Each style and its variants are HTML, CSS and JSON files, checked against schemas when the site is built. Each variant's CSS is scoped to its own faces at build time, so variants can reuse class names without leaking styles. Adding a variant needs no code.
how.data.title: Your data
how.data.p1: Your card is saved in your browser's storage and nowhere else. When you upload a drawing, a Web Worker turns it into a die-cut sticker (white border, flat shadow) on your device; the image is never sent anywhere.
how.data.p2: A saved card is a small JSON document. Any document the editor reads is treated as untrusted: its size is capped, keys that could tamper with JavaScript objects are refused, it's validated against a schema compiled at build time, and its texts only ever go into the page as plain text.
how.exports.title: Exports
how.exports.p1: Each face is rendered from its own page element to a 1134 × 661 PNG, which is 96 × 56 mm with 3 mm of bleed at 300 dpi, and the PNG is marked as 300 dpi. The print PDF puts both faces on two pages of that size. Safari's engine needed a few fixes to export faithfully, each covered by a test that checks the exported pixels.
how.exports.p2: For print shops that want vector text, a command-line tool prints a saved card with Chromium, with real, selectable text and embedded fonts. In CI, every variant is exported in Chromium and WebKit and checked for print: size and dpi, both QR codes decode exactly (the main one even at half resolution), nothing covers them, at most four fonts per face, and every character exists in its font.
how.security.title: Security
how.security.p1: A Content Security Policy lets the page load scripts, styles, fonts and images only from its own origin, and tests check that nothing is ever requested from anywhere else. Exports are ordinary downloads made on your device.
how.security.p2: A test-only hook used by the end-to-end tests is compiled out of the published site, and CI checks that no trace of it ships. Published images carry pixel data only, with no metadata. Every dependency is pinned and audited, and every change is scanned for secrets.
how.quality.title: Quality
how.quality.p1: Nothing is built before its requirements and design are written and approved. Every change starts as an issue, lands on its own branch as signed, conventional commits, goes through a pull request that says how it was verified, and merges only when CI passes. History is never rewritten: mistakes are fixed with new commits.
how.quality.p2: Tests run in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit: unit tests, end-to-end tests that drive every editor control through the interface in both languages, screenshots of each card compared with the original prototype, and automated accessibility checks.
how.releases.title: Releases
how.releases.p1: Work is planned in milestones, and each milestone ends in a release. release-please keeps a release pull request open with the next version and its changelog, written from the commit messages. Merging it tags the version and publishes the release.
how.releases.p2: The site deploys from the main branch only after CI has passed on that exact commit.
